q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the maximum speed in cities, towns and villages?
a: 50 km/h
e: No sign: 50 in town, 80 elsewhere.
s: Where there are no posted speed limits, the maximum speed is 50 km/h in cities, towns and villages, and 80 km/h elsewhere.

q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the maximum speed outside cities, towns and villages?
a: 80 km/h
e: No sign: 80 out of town, 50 in town.
s: and 80 km/h elsewhere

q: What is the minimum safe following distance in ideal conditions?
a: 2 seconds
e: At least 2 seconds behind the vehicle ahead, and more in bad conditions.
s: A safe following distance is at least two seconds behind the vehicle in front of you.

q: About how often should you check your mirrors?
a: Every 5 seconds or so
e: Keep your eyes moving: scan ahead and to the sides, and check mirrors about every 5 seconds.
s: checking your mirrors every five seconds or so

q: Picture the steering wheel as a clock. Where should your hands be?
a: At 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock
e: 9 and 3.
s: Picture the steering wheel as a clock and place your hands at nine o'clock and three o'clock.

q: A police officer directing traffic waves you through, but your light is red. What do you do?
a: Follow the officer's directions
e: Police directions overrule traffic lights and signs.
s: When police officers are directing traffic, you must follow their directions, even if the directions are different from traffic lights or signs.

q: You're pulling out from a parking spot at the curb. Who goes first?
a: Traffic on the road: signal, check, and pull out only when it's safe
w: You do, if you're already moving
e: Before moving from a parked position, signal and check for traffic. Pull out only when it's safe.
s: Before moving from a parked position, always signal and check for traffic, pulling out only when it is safe to do so.

q: A pedestrian is crossing the road ahead of you. There's no crosswalk. What should you usually do?
a: Yield to the pedestrian
w: Speed up to pass before they reach your lane
e: Drivers must take care around pedestrians. In most cases, that means yielding.
s: In most cases, that means yielding to the pedestrian.

q: Which statement about the 2-second rule is TRUE?
a: It's the MINIMUM following distance, for ideal conditions only
e: You need more space in bad weather, behind motorcycles or trucks, or with a heavy load.
s: Remember that the two-second rule gives a minimum following distance. It applies only to ideal driving conditions.

q: In which situation is a 2-second following distance enough?
a: Following a car on a dry road in ideal conditions
e: Bad weather, motorcycles, large trucks and heavy loads all need extra space.
s: You will need extra space in certain situations, such as bad weather, when following motorcycles or large trucks, or when carrying a heavy load.

q: Is it legal to drive with a radar detector (speed-measuring warning device) in your car?
a: No: it's illegal, and you can be fined and get demerit points
w: Yes, as long as you don't speed
e: Radar detectors are illegal in Ontario (3 demerit points).
s: Speed measuring warning devices are illegal. If you get caught driving with such a device, you will be fined and accumulate demerit points.

q: Your turn signals are broken. What is the hand signal for a RIGHT turn?
a: Left arm out the window, bent UP at the elbow
w: Left arm bent DOWN at the elbow
Right arm out the passenger window
e: Left arm: straight out = left turn, bent up = right turn, bent down = slow or stop.
s: a driver flashing right-turn signal and making hand signal for right turn-left arm extended out and bent up at right angle

q: When should you NOT use cruise control?
a: On wet, icy or slippery roads, in heavy traffic, or when you're tired
e: Cruise control can save fuel on the highway, but not in those conditions.
s: there are some circumstances in which cruise control should not be used, such as adverse driving conditions (wet, icy or slippery roads), in heavy traffic or when you are feeling fatigued

q: It's raining hard and traffic is heavy. The speed limit is 80 km/h. How fast should you drive?
a: Below the limit, at a speed that lets you stop safely
w: Faster than traffic, to get out of the rain sooner
As fast as the car in front
e: The posted limit is a maximum, not a target. Slow down in bad conditions.
s: This means driving below the maximum speed in bad weather, in heavy traffic or in construction zones.

q: A police officer signals you to pull over. What should you do?
a: Pull as far to the right as is safe, stop completely, and stay in your car
w: Get out and walk to the police car
Keep driving to the next exit
Stop in your lane right away
e: Stay in your vehicle and wait for the officer.
s: you must pull over as far to the right as you safely can and come to a complete stop. Stay in your vehicle and wait for the police officer.

q: On a multi-lane road, which lane should you normally drive in?
a: The right-hand lane, unless you're turning left or passing
w: The left lane, because it's faster
e: Keep right, especially if you're driving slower than other traffic.
s: Keep to the right of the road or in the right-hand lane on multi-lane roads unless you want to turn left or pass another vehicle.

q: How do you check that you're at least 2 seconds behind the car ahead?
a: When its rear passes a marker, count "one thousand and one, one thousand and two" until your front reaches the marker
w: Count the car lengths between you
e: If you reach the marker before you finish counting, you're too close.
s: If you reach the marker before you count "one thousand and two," you are following too closely.

q: Your brake lights and turn signals stop working. How should you signal?
a: Use hand and arm signals
e: Hand and arm signals are the backup.
s: If your turn signals and brake lights are not working, use hand and arm signals.

q: How should you adjust your seat?
a: So you can see over the wheel and hood, and see the ground about 4 metres ahead, with elbows slightly bent
w: So your arms are fully straight
So your chin is on the wheel
e: Your feet should reach the pedals easily.
s: You should be able to see the ground four metres in front of the vehicle.

q: When must you signal?
a: Before stopping, slowing down, turning, changing lanes, leaving the road, or pulling out from a parked position
w: Only when other cars are around
e: Signal well before you act, and make sure the way is clear. Signalling alone isn't enough.
s: Use your turn signals and brake lights to signal before stopping, slowing down, turning, changing lanes, leaving the road or moving out from a parked position.

q: Driving too slowly for no reason, so you block normal traffic, is…
a: An offence: don't block the normal and reasonable movement of traffic
e: Unnecessary slow driving = 2 demerit points.
s: Do not block the normal and reasonable movement of traffic.

q: Defensive driving is based on which three ideas?
a: Visibility, space and communication
e: See and be seen, keep space around you, and let others know what you're doing.
s: Defensive driving is based on three ideas: visibility, space and communication.

q: Why do school zones and construction zones often have lower speed limits?
a: To protect children and people working on or near the road
e: Obey the lower limit.
s: School zones and construction zones often have lower speed limits to protect children and those who work on or near the road.

q: A police officer asks you to pull over and you don't. What can happen?
a: A fine, a licence suspension, or even prison
w: Nothing, if you didn't see them
e: Failing to stop for police is 7 demerit points, and your licence can be suspended for at least 5 years.
s: If you do not obey a police officer’s direction to pull over, you risk being fined, having your licence suspended or even serving time in prison.

q: You should under all conditions drive at a speed which will allow you to:
a: Stop within a safe distance.
e: Official MTO sample question. There's no fixed distance: it depends on conditions.
s: but always drive at a speed that will let you stop safely
